title: Always copy R memory in torch_tensor() for already-contiguous arrays
description:
`torch_tensor()` can return a tensor that points straight at the R object's memory instead of a copy. If R later garbage collects the array, the tensor reads freed memory (intermittent NaNs / wrong values), and in-place ops on the tensor write into the R object.

### Reproduction (torch 0.16.3, CPU)

```r
library(torch)
x <- matrix(c(1, 2, 3), ncol = 1)
a <- torch_tensor(x, dtype = torch_float64())
b <- torch_tensor(x, dtype = torch_float64())
a$storage()$data_ptr() == b$storage()$data_ptr()
#> TRUE   # both tensors share R's memory

a$add_(1)
x[, 1]
#> 2 3 4  # in-place op on the tensor modified the R object

# control: with the default float32 the cast copies
a <- torch_tensor(x); b <- torch_tensor(x)
a$storage()$data_ptr() == b$storage()$data_ptr()
#> FALSE
```

### Cause

`create_tensor_from_atomic()` wraps R's memory with `from_blob` and relies on `contiguous()` to make the copy, cloning explicitly only for 1-d input. But R arrays where every dimension but one has size 1 (`n x 1`, `1 x n`, `n x 1 x 1`, ...) already count as contiguous, so `contiguous()` returns the same tensor. If no dtype conversion follows (double + `torch_float64()`, integer + `torch_int32()`, `integer64` by default), `$to()` doesn't copy either.

### Fix

Clone whenever the wrapped tensor is already contiguous, otherwise let `contiguous()` copy. This keeps a single copy in every case and covers the old 1-d special case. Tests added in `test-tensor.R` for several shapes and dtypes, plus a NEWS entry.

I found this while debugging intermittent NaN losses in a package built on torch; the workaround there was to `$clone()` every tensor created from an R matrix.

title: Accept a tensor as the first argument of $to() (#1060)
description:
PyTorch allows `x.to(y)` to convert `x` to the dtype and device of `y`. In R this needed `x$to(other = y)`, and `x$to(y)` failed with "Can't convert argument:dtype". Treat a tensor passed as `dtype` as `other`, and pass `memory_format` through on that path instead of silently dropping it.

Do the same for `nn_module`'s `$to()`, where `module$to(y)` failed too. `module$to(y)` and `module$to(tensor = y)` now take both the dtype and the device from `y` like PyTorch's `_parse_to()`. Previously `tensor` was forwarded only for floating point parameters, so integer buffers stayed on their old device, and an integer `y` silently cast float parameters to integer.

title: Fix RNNs on sequences packed with enforce_sorted = TRUE (#1156)
description:
When sequences are packed with `enforce_sorted = TRUE`, the `PackedSequence`'s sorted/unsorted indices are undefined tensors. The R getters called `$add()` on them to make them 1-based, which failed with "Expected a proper Tensor but got None", so every RNN on such input errored.

The getters now return `NULL` for undefined indices, which is what the RNN forward pass already expects for "no permutation". `new_packed_sequence()` maps `NULL` back to an undefined tensor.

title: Deduplicate named_parameters()/named_buffers() with recursive = FALSE…
description:
… (#988)

When the same tensor is registered under two names, `$named_parameters()` returned it once with `recursive = TRUE` but twice with `recursive = FALSE`. Optimizers and anything else iterating over parameters should see each tensor once.

Both methods now deduplicate in either mode, and take a `remove_duplicate` argument as in PyTorch. The tracer passes `remove_duplicate = FALSE` so that traced script modules keep registering every alias as before. `$parameters` and `$buffers` now delegate to these methods instead of duplicating the logic. With the default `remove_duplicate = TRUE`, children are still collected through their `$parameters`/`$buffers` fields, so subclasses that override those (or `named_parameters()` with the old signature) keep working.

title: Fix torch_arange() dropping the end point for string dtypes (#1063)
description:
`torch_arange()` includes `end` by bumping it by one step when the dtype is an integer type. That check uses `is_integer_dtype()`, which returned `FALSE` for a dtype given as a string such as `"long"`, so `torch_arange(1, 3, dtype = "long")` returned `1 2` instead of `1 2 3`.

`is_integer_dtype()` now also accepts strings, parsing them with the same C++ code that parses string dtypes when creating tensors, so unknown strings still error and every dtype name libtorch accepts keeps working.

title: Call from jit operators
description:
This would allow calling JIT registered operators without the need to manually create wrappers in C++.
For future reference:

We need to port the logic here into R: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/47834679ba2f869e66450a74e2add4c04f0006e9/torch/csrc/jit/python/pybind_utils.h#L874-L947

Once we have it, next step should be similar to simply calling the found operation:

https://cs.github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/47834679ba2f869e66450a74e2add4c04f0006e9/torch/csrc/jit/python/pybind_utils.h#L1182

title: Add ... to the as_array() generic
description: `as_array()` had the signature `function(x)`, so methods defined in other packages could not take extra arguments without failing R CMD check's generic/method consistency check. Add `...` to the generic and both methods; the default method forwards it to `base::as.array()`.

title: Fix backward through max/min/sort/topk/max_pool with indices (#1185)
description:
The R wrappers shift the returned indices to 1-based with `$add_()`. For `torch_max()`, `torch_min()`, `torch_sort()`, `torch_topk()`, the `$sort()` and `$topk()` methods and the max pooling `*_with_indices()` functions, autograd saves that same index tensor for the backward pass, so the in-place shift bumps its version counter and `$backward()` fails with "modified by an inplace operation".

Shift out of place instead. The `_out` variants keep the in-place shift because they have to write into the caller's tensor, and argmax/argmin/argsort keep it because their outputs are never saved for backward.

title: Use scaled dot product attention in nn_multihead_attention when need_…
description:
## Use fused attention in `nn_multihead_attention()` and match PyTorch

`nn_multihead_attention()` and `nnf_multi_head_attention_forward()` now use fused attention kernels and give the same results as PyTorch 2.8.

### Performance
- **`need_weights = FALSE`** uses the fused `torch_scaled_dot_product_attention()`. With `batch_first = TRUE`, the inputs are no longer transposed and the output is contiguous.
- **New `is_causal` argument**: a hint that `attn_mask` is the causal mask. Without a key padding mask, the fused attention then applies the causal mask itself, which allows the fastest kernels. `nn_transformer_encoder_layer()` passes it on.
- **Fused native inference path**: in evaluation mode and without gradients, self-attention with `batch_first = TRUE` uses `torch__native_multi_head_attention()` under PyTorch's conditions, with one exception. Masked attention with `need_weights = FALSE` uses the fused scaled dot product attention instead, because the native kernel is up to 3.5× slower with a mask.
- Self-attention is detected by tensor identity (as in PyTorch), instead of comparing the values of `query`, `key` and `value` with `torch_equal()` in every forward pass.
- The in-projection weights are split with `$split()` / `$chunk()` instead of R indexing.

### Fixes
- `add_zero_attn = TRUE` failed: the zero attention was added to thevalues.
- Integer (e.g. `uint8`) masks were added to the attention scores instead of being treated as boolean masks, as documented.
- Non-contiguous masks failed with `need_weights = FALSE`, and mask now work like in PyTorch.
- With `kdim` or `vdim`, `avg_weights` was ignored.

### Checked against PyTorch
A harness compared R torch with PyTorch 2.8.0 (the bundled libtorch ations**, comparing outputs, attention weights and all gradients. Itcovers:
- the module and functional interfaces, and the encoder layer
- self, cross and encoder-decoder attention, including equal but not identical inputs
- bool, float, uint8, 2D and 3D masks, causal masks with and without masks (including fully masked rows)
- `add_bias_kv`, `add_zero_attn`, `kdim`/`vdim`, `bias = FALSE`, `static_k`/`static_v`
- `batch_first`, train and eval mode, with and without gradients, fld arguments

Results:
- **CPU:** all cases match except 2 (below); max abs diff 3.8e-6 in float32, 3.6e-15 in float64. Dropout gives the same results as PyTorch for the same seed.
- **CUDA:** the same result against the CPU reference; max abs diff
- **Before this PR**, `main` matched in 6,007 cases and the first version of this PR in 10,647. The rest came from the bugs above.

Intended differences from PyTorch:
- **Fully masked rows in masked inference (2 cases):** in inference nd a mask, rows where every key is masked give 0 instead of NaN. This comes from using the fused attention instead of the native kernel, and it's what PyTorch itself returns in training mode.
- **`is_causal` with an extra key (131 cases):** with `is_causal = Tdd_zero_attn` (and `need_weights = FALSE`), PyTorch's causal maskalso hides the added key. That makes PyTorch's result differ from the same mask without the hint, and from `need_weights = TRUE`. R keeps the mask, so its result is the same in all three cases. These cases were compared against PyTor

title: Guard the cudatoolkit lib_path() call during startup
description:
`load_cudatoolkit_libs()` calls the `cuda*` package's `lib_path()` unguarded, so any error raised there propagates out of `.onLoad` and is reported as torch failing to start.

On a machine with a `cuda*` package installed:

```
$ R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=NULL Rscript --vanilla -e 'loadNamespace("torch")'
ℹ torch failed to start, restart your R session to try again.
ℹ You might need to reinstall torch using `install_torch()`
✖ could not find function "packageName"
```

The reported fault is torch; the actual fault is in the toolkit package. That particular trigger is mlverse/cudatoolkit#5, and `R CMD check` clears `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES` for its whole driver process, so it fires there too.

Not hypothetical: the same signature is in [#1463 (comment, 2026-07-05)](https://github.com/mlverse/torch/issues/1463#issuecomment-4887670975), where it outlives the symlink workaround that thread is otherwise about. For a package that touches torch at load time the cost is not a NOTE, it is three `R CMD check` WARNINGs and `.onLoad failed in loadNamespace()`.

### The existing guard cannot fire

```r
lib_path <- getExportedValue(pkg_name, "lib_path")()
if (!dir.exists(lib_path)) return(invisible(FALSE))
```

`cuda*::lib_path()` is `system.file("lib", package = ..., mustWork = TRUE)`, which errors rather than returning `""` when the directory is missing, so control never arrives at `dir.exists()` with a bad path.

### Change

Catch the error, warn naming the toolkit package, and continue without preloading. This matches how the `dyn.load()` calls further down are already handled.

Verified against the real failing call:

```
# before
ERROR propagates: could not find function "packageName"

# after
Warning message:
ℹ Skipping CUDA library preload from cuda12.8.
✖ could not find function "packageName"
guard returned: NULL -> caller returns invisible(FALSE)
```

`cli::cli_warn()` was checked in the same `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=NULL` environment, so the handler does not reintroduce the failure it reports.

Startup then continues with whatever libraries remain available. Whether that lands on a working session depends on the build: a CPU build, or one with another usable CUDA source, starts; a CUDA build that needed the skipped libraries still fails, but names the toolkit package rather than torch.

### One question

Possibly also upstream of #1463's *original* symptom. `load_cudatoolkit_libs()` exists to `dyn.load()` the toolkit's CUDA libraries before `cpp_lantern_init()`, so if it aborts or silently no-ops, `liblantern.so` has nothing to resolve `libcudart.so.12` against. Not asserting it — the original trace there reaches `cpp_lantern_init()`, so the preload returned rather than errored in that invocation.

title: Preserve tensor dtype when the left operand is an R scalar
description:
## Problem

Arithmetic with an R scalar on the **left** silently promotes reduced-precision and integer tensors:

```r
t <- torch_ones(3, dtype = torch_bfloat16())
(t - 1)$dtype   # BFloat16, as expected
(1 - t)$dtype   # Float  <- silently upcast
(1 - torch_ones(3, dtype = torch_long()))$dtype   # Float (PyTorch returns Long)
```

In Python, `1 - t` keeps `t`'s dtype because Python scalars participate weakly in type promotion.

This surfaced as a hard failure in a bfloat16 attention stack: an additive mask built with `1 - attention_mask` came out float32, and CUDA's fused `scaled_dot_product_attention` rejects a bias whose dtype doesn't match the query ("invalid dtype for bias - should match query's dtype").

## Cause

The operator methods wrap a non-tensor lhs with `torch_tensor(e1, ...)`, which yields a **dimensioned** (length-1, 1-d) tensor of the default dtype. libtorch lets dimensioned tensors dictate promotion, so float32 wins over bfloat16/int64. The rhs case never hits this path: `torch_sub(tensor, 1)` takes the Tensor-Scalar overload, which promotes weakly.

## Fix

Wrap length-1 numeric/logical lhs operands with `torch_scalar_tensor()` instead. 0-dim tensors promote weakly, exactly like Python scalars, so:

- `1 - bf16` stays BFloat16, `2 * half` stays Half
- `1L + long` stays Long, `5L %% long` stays Long
- `1L / long` still promotes to the default float dtype (division semantics unchanged)
- `c(1, 2, 3) - bf16` still promotes to Float (dimensioned vectors keep their old behavior)
- `NA`, `NaN`, logical, and integer scalars behave as before (verified against `torch_tensor()` conversions)

Applied to the seven arithmetic ops (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `^`, `%%`, `%/%`). Comparison operators share the wrapping pattern but return bool, so they're left untouched.

The regression test fails 4 assertions before the patch and passes after; the rest of `test-operators.R` is unchanged (149 passing before and after, CPU and CUDA checked).

title: Respect torch_set_num_threads() in the backward pass
description:
The problem is the following: torch has a thread-pool and calls to `$backward()` are run in these threads. When the thread pool is created, every thread reads the main thread's number of threads and sets it. However, if we afterwards change the number of threads via `torch_set_num_threads()`, the threads in the pool don't update their threads. This is changed now.

Previously, `$backward()` did use the wrong number of theads when the number of threads changed during the session.

The text below is created by Claude:

### Verification

5 iterations of `torch_mm(x, w)$exp()$sum()$backward()` with 4000×4000 tensors on a 32-core Linux machine. The table shows CPU time divided by wall time (1.0 means one thread):

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| A: `torch_set_num_threads(1)` before the first backward | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| B: first backward with the default (16 threads) | 14.8 | 14.8 |
| B: then `torch_set_num_threads(1)` | **7.2** | **1.0** |

There is no automated test. The backward worker threads cannot be observed from R, because R hooks run on the main thread.

title: fix: keep torch_scalar_tensor() a leaf when requires_grad = TRUE
description:
`torch_scalar_tensor()` created the tensor with `requires_grad = TRUE` and then called `$squeeze()` on it. Since `$squeeze()` is a tracked autograd op, the returned tensor was no longer a leaf, so `.grad` was never populated after `backward()` (as sebffischer diagnosed in the issue thread).

This fix squeezes first and only enables `requires_grad` afterwards via `$requires_grad_()`, for the non-tensor-input branch (the tensor-input branch already called `$requires_grad_()` last and was unaffected). dtype/device handling is unchanged.

Added a regression test covering both branches (plain value and tensor input) that checks `is_leaf` and the gradient value after `backward()`.

Fixes #1368.

title: Add experimental Lantern-backed Tensor API
description:
## What

Adds a `torch::experimental::Tensor` C++ facade backed by Lantern calls. It supports direct use in Rcpp exports, including fluent code such as `input.relu().reshape({-1})`.

The initial handwritten facade covers core Tensor behavior and conversions, while generated methods expose the broader Tensor namespace from `src/gen-namespace.cpp`. The generator currently emits 758 overloads and audits coverage of 815 public Lantern Tensor entry points.

## Why

Packages using torch currently receive handle types but cannot write a LibTorch-style Tensor API without linking directly against LibTorch. This facade keeps the existing Lantern ABI boundary while providing a familiar C++ interface.

## Impact

- Adds an opt-in API under `torch::experimental`; existing APIs are unchanged.
- Resolves Lantern symbols through registered R C-callables.
- Adds representative runtime tests for Tensor input/output, chaining, generated methods, integer arguments, and boolean returns.
- Adds a freshness and coverage test for generated methods.

## Validation

- `python3 tools/generate-experimental-tensor.py --check` — passes (758 generated overloads; 815 Lantern Tensor entry points covered).
- `testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-experimental-cpp-codegen.R")` — passes.
- `testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-experimental-cpp-api.R")` — passes all 5 runtime assertions against the installed branch and configured Lantern runtime.
- The package was installed from this branch with `BUILD_LANTERN=1 R CMD INSTALL .` before running the tests.

title: fix: interpret ignore_index as a 1-based class index
description:
`with-indices.R` exists to translate R's 1-based indexing into libtorch's 0-based one. It converted the `target` of the NLL and cross entropy losses but forwarded `ignore_index` unchanged, even though `ignore_index` names a target value and is compared against the already-converted target inside libtorch.

As a result `ignore_index = k` ignored class `k - 1`, and the last class could not be ignored at all. Nothing caught this because the default `-100` is a sentinel that matches no target in either convention, and there was no test for the argument.

`to_index_ignore_index()` now applies the same shift to any value that can be a 1-based class index, and leaves negative sentinels alone. `0` becomes an error rather than silently ignoring the first class.

The documented target range was `0 <= target <= C-1`, copied from PyTorch, which `to_index_tensor()` has always rejected; it now reads `1 <= target <= C`.

man/ was updated by hand because roxygen2 has to load the package to run.

title: fix: build the is_causal mask on the device of the input
description:
nn_transformer_encoder_layer()$forward() creates the causal mask with torch_ones(), which places it on the default device. Once the module and its input are on the GPU, the attention is then given a CPU mask and fails with a device mismatch, so `is_causal = TRUE` is unusable outside the CPU.

The mask is now created on the device of `src`. On the CPU this is a no-op, as `src$device` is the default device there.

The existing GPU test does not cover `is_causal`, which is how this went unnoticed; a regression test is added for both `batch_first` layouts, checking that the flag agrees with passing the same mask explicitly. It uses skip_if_cuda_not_available() rather than the `if (cuda_is_available())` of the test above it, so that it reports as skipped instead of as an empty test.

title: fix: multihead attention without bias, and one cycle linear annealing
description:
Both bugs were found while auditing mlr3torch, which exposes the affected options as tunable hyperparameters.

* `nnf_multi_head_attention_forward()` failed with `object 'k' not found` when `bias = FALSE` and `query` was not the same tensor as `key`, i.e. for cross-attention and encoder-decoder attention. In the branch that handles a shared key and value, the key/value projection was computed inside the `if (!is.null(b_))` block, so both `k` and `v` were left unassigned when there was no bias. The projection is now computed unconditionally and only the bias slice remains conditional, matching the surrounding branches.

* `lr_one_cycle()` failed with `attempt to apply non-function` when `anneal_strategy = "linear"`, because the annealing function was assigned to `self.anneal_func` rather than `self$anneal_func` and therefore never set. The "cos" branch on the preceding line is spelled correctly.

Both are covered by new regression tests, which fail without the corresponding fix.

title: Prepend install lib dir to PATH on Windows so cuDNN sub-DLLs resolve
description:
Addresses the Windows cuDNN DLL load failure tracked in #1287 (the `Could not locate cudnn_graph64_9.dll` reports there).

## Problem

On Windows CUDA installs, cuDNN-backed ops fail at runtime even though every cuDNN 9 DLL is present in `<install>/torch/lib`:

```r
library(torch)
x <- torch_randn(1, 3, 16, 16, device = "cuda")
w <- torch_randn(4, 3, 3, 3, device = "cuda")
nnf_conv2d(x, w)
#> Could not locate cudnn_graph64_9.dll. Please make sure it is in your library path!
#> Invalid handle. Cannot load symbol cudnnCreate
```

`cuda_is_available()` is `TRUE` and non-cuDNN CUDA ops (e.g. `torch_mm`) work. This lines up with the diagnosis in #1287 that the loader isn't finding `torch/lib`.

## Cause

cuDNN 9 is split across several DLLs. `lanternLoadLibrary` loads `lantern.dll` with `LoadLibraryEx(..., LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS)`, which resolves the static dependency chain (libtorch, `cudnn64_9.dll`) from the install lib dir. But `cudnn64_9.dll` then lazily loads `cudnn_graph64_9.dll` by name, and that load does not find the install lib dir unless it is on `PATH`.

## Fix

Prepend the install lib dir to `PATH` at load on Windows, so cuDNN's by-name sub-DLL loads resolve. This mirrors the existing `load_cudatoolkit_libs()` handling, which already does the same `Sys.setenv(PATH = ...)` for the separate cudatoolkit-package case. The prepend is idempotent, so repeated `library()`/reload calls don't grow `PATH`.

## Verification

Prepending `torch/lib` to `PATH` resolves the failure on torch 0.17.0 / libtorch 2.8.0+cu126, Windows 10, R 4.6.0 and R-devel: `nnf_conv2d` and a full `torch_scaled_dot_product_attention` forward then run and return correct results on GPU.

Refs #1287

title: Add POSIX shared memory transport for multi-worker dataloaders
description:
## Summary

- Adds a new IPC transport option for multi-worker dataloaders using POSIX shared memory (`shm_open`/`mmap`), enabled via `options(torch.dataloader_use_shm = TRUE)`.
- The SHM path performs **1 memcpy** on the producer (tensor → SHM) and **0 copies** on the consumer (`from_blob` aliases the mapped memory), compared to serialize + pipe transfer + deserialize in the default path.
- Adds `r_dataptr_ro()` in the C++ layer to avoid triggering ALTREP copy-on-write when reading buffers via `torch::from_blob`.

### Benchmark results (excluding worker startup)

| Config | Default | SHM | Speedup | MB/batch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 500x1K, bs=32 | 0.234s | 0.175s | 1.34x | 0.1 |
| 200x50K, bs=64 | 0.113s | 0.063s | 1.79x | 12.2 |
| 200x100K, bs=64 | 0.129s | 0.090s | 1.43x | 24.4 |
| 100x500K, bs=64 | 0.050s | 0.022s | 2.27x | 122.1 |
| 100x1M, bs=32 | 0.736s | 0.425s | 1.73x | 122.1 |

## Test plan

If you are running on GitHub hosted runners this will just work, if you are using self-hosted runners make sure, that your runners are up to date. If you followed the normal installation instructions your self-hosted runner will keep itself updated.

This release also removes the deprecated input server-url which was used to download uv releases from a different server. The manifest-file input supersedes that functionality by adding a flexible way to define available versions and where they should be downloaded from.

Fixes

  • The action now respects when the environment variable UV_CACHE_DIR is already set and does not overwrite it. It now also finds cache-dir settings in config files if you set them.
  • Some users encountered problems that cache pruning took forever because they had some uv processes running in the background. Starting with uv version 0.8.24 this action uses uv cache prune --ci --force to ignore the running processes
  • If you just want to install uv but not have it available in path, this action now respects UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH
  • Some other actions also set the env var UV_CACHE_DIR. This action can now deal with that but as this could lead to unwanted behavior in some edgecases a warning is now displayed.

Improvements

If you are using minimum version specifiers for the version of uv to install for example

[tool.uv]
required-version = ">=0.8.17"

This action now detects that and directly uses the latest version. Previously it would download all available releases from the uv repo to determine the highest matching candidate for the version specifier, which took much more time.

If you are using other specifiers like 0.8.x this action still needs to download all available releases because the specifier defines an upper bound (not 0.9.0 or later) and "latest" would possibly not satisfy that.

title: Add Python comparison to CPU cache benchmark
description:
## Summary

title: Replace R_RunPendingFinalizers with weak reference flag check
description:
## Summary

- Replace `R_RunPendingFinalizers()` + `Rf_duplicate()` in `operator_sexp_tensor` with R's weak reference API
- Store an `R_MakeWeakRefC` weak reference in TensorImpl's pyobj slot instead of the raw SEXP
- Check the `READY_TO_FINALIZE` flag (bit 0 of `gp`, set by R's GC in `CheckFinalizers()` before finalizers run) to detect stale keys without forcing all pending finalizers to execute

### Why

`R_RunPendingFinalizers()` is called on **every** tensor return that hits the cached SEXP path (primarily in-place operations like `mul_`, `add_`, etc.). It forces execution of all pending finalizers across the entire R session, which is unnecessary work. This is particularly costly in tight loops like optimizer steps.

### How it works

R's GC processes weak references in two phases:
1. `CheckFinalizers()` — sets `READY_TO_FINALIZE` flag on weak refs whose keys are unreachable
2. `RunFinalizers()` — clears keys/values and runs finalizer callbacks

By checking the flag (via `LEVELS(weakref) & 1`), we can detect that a key has been scheduled for collection **before** the finalizer runs — closing the race window that `R_RunPendingFinalizers()` was solving.

## Test plan

- [x] Basic tensor operations (in-place and new-tensor) work correctly
- [x] GC stress test (500 iterations with `gc()` between ops) passes
- [x] Neural network forward/backward passes
- [x] Optimizer step works

title: Add CPU block cache to compensate for R's deferred GC
description:
## Summary

- Adds a CPU block cache that reuses freed tensor memory blocks, avoiding expensive `mmap`/`munmap` syscalls caused by R's deferred garbage collection
- New exported API: `set_cpu_allocator_config()` and `cpu_cache_flush()`
- Updates the memory management vignette with documentation on the CPU cache

## Motivation

Python frees tensors immediately via reference counting, so the system allocator efficiently reuses memory. R uses garbage collection, meaning dead tensors accumulate until GC runs. For large tensors (> ~1 MB), this forces repeated `mmap`/`munmap` system calls instead of reusing blocks — causing significant overhead in training loops.

The CPU block cache intercepts freed blocks and holds them in an in-process pool keyed by size. Subsequent allocations of the same size skip the system allocator entirely. The cache is flushed automatically after each GC cycle and on OOM.

## Benchmark results

### Training loop (latent=5000)

2-layer NN (100 → 5000 → 1), Adam optimizer, 1000 steps, 5 reps. CPU only, Apple M3.

| | **mean** | **se** |
|---|---|---|
| **R (cache enabled)** | 4.214s | 0.065s |
| **R (cache disabled)** | 7.584s | 0.024s |
| **Python 2.8.0** | 4.440s | 0.015s |

R with cache is **5% faster than Python** and **1.80x faster** than without cache.

### Speedup by hidden layer size

The cache benefit scales with tensor size — small tensors use heap malloc (no benefit), large tensors use mmap (significant benefit):

| Latent | Cache enabled | Cache disabled | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 0.64s | 0.63s | 0.99x |
| 50 | 0.80s | 0.84s | 1.06x |
| 100 | 0.87s | 0.96s | 1.11x |
| 500 | 1.32s | 1.95s | 1.47x |
| 1000 | 1.60s | 2.80s | 1.75x |
| 2000 | 2.43s | 4.26s | 1.76x |
| 5000 | 4.32s | 7.83s | 1.81x |

Benchmark scripts: `bench/benchmark_cpu_cache/`

## How it works

- On free: if caching is enabled and the cache isn't full, the block is stored in a hashmap (`size → vector<void*>`) instead of being returned to the OS
- On allocate: check the hashmap for an exact size match before calling `alloc_cpu`
- After GC: flush the entire cache to return memory to the OS
- On OOM: flush cache, retry, then trigger full GC and retry again

## Configuration

```r
# Adjust at runtime
set_cpu_allocator_config(
  cache_enabled = TRUE,        # default
  cache_max_size_mb = 4000,    # matches GC threshold
  cache_min_block_size = 1024  # 1 KB minimum
)

# Manually release cached memory
cpu_cache_flush()

# Or via options before library(torch)
options(torch.cpu_cache_enabled = TRUE)
options(torch.cpu_cache_max_size_mb = 4000)
```

title: Optimize dynamic dispatcher performance
description:
## Summary

Overhaul the dynamic dispatch pipeline so that generated code bypasses the generic `call_c_function` R dispatcher entirely. All ~2,800 generated functions now use one of three fast paths:

- **Direct call** (84% of namespace, 80% of methods): single-overload functions call the C++ wrapper directly — no dispatch at all
- **Inline R if/else** (4% of namespace, 13% of methods): 2-overload functions with one multi-type arg use a generated type check in R
- **C++ dispatcher** (12% of namespace, 7% of methods): remaining multi-overload functions dispatch entirely in C++ via a generated per-function dispatcher

The generic `call_c_function` / `do_call` / `.dispatch_cache` code path is removed.

### Micro-benchmarks (2×2 tensors, Apple M3)

| function | dispatch path | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `torch_matmul` | direct call | 6.76µs | 1.44µs | **79%** |
| `torch_add` | inline if/else | 6.76µs | 2.01µs | **70%** |
| `torch_div` | C++ dispatcher | 6.76µs | 2.34µs | **65%** |

### End-to-end GPT-2 benchmark (minhub, CPU, Apple M3)

| model | CRAN 0.17.0 | this branch | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tiny (1 layer, 64-dim) | 1.42ms | 1.15ms | **19%** |
| Small (2 layers, 128-dim) | 2.85ms | 2.48ms | **13%** |

### Changes

- **R/codegen-utils.R**: Remove `call_c_function`, `do_call`, `.dispatch_cache`. Add `is_tensor_dispatch()` / `is_int64_dispatch()` helpers for inline dispatch.
- **src/codegen.cpp**: Remove `create_fn_name`, `cpp_make_function_name`, `cpp_clean_names`, `cpp_suffix`. Keep `cpp_arg_to_torch_type` (used by C++ dispatchers).
- **tools/torchgen/R/r.R**: Generate direct calls (single overload), inline if/else (2-overload), or C++ dispatcher calls (3+ overloads). Replace `make_cpp_function_name` dependency on C++ with pure-R implementation.
- **tools/torchgen/R/cpp.R**: Generate per-function C++ dispatchers for multi-overload groups.

## Test plan

- [x] Full test suite: `[ FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 71 | PASS 2971 ]`
- [x] Micro-benchmarks in `bench/bench-dispatch.R`
- [x] End-to-end GPT-2 benchmark in `bench/bench-gpt2.R`
- [x] Codegen is idempotent (regenerating produces no diff)

title: Add move semantics and reduce shared_ptr copy overhead
description:
## Summary
- **`get_shared()` returns `const&`** instead of by value, eliminating one atomic refcount increment per call
- **Add default move constructors** to all 39 `XPtrTorch` subclasses that declare explicit copy constructors. C++ suppresses the implicit move constructor when a copy constructor is user-declared, so without these, passing temporaries falls back to copying (atomic refcount ops) instead of free pointer swaps
- **Add default copy/move assignment operators** alongside move constructors (required by the Rule of Five — declaring a move constructor suppresses implicit copy assignment)
- **`make_xptr` uses `std::move`** to avoid a redundant `shared_ptr` copy when wrapping objects into R external pointers

title: Bump actions/download-artifact from 7 to 8
description:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 7 to 8.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v7...v8.0.0

title: Split GPU testing into Docker-based build/test workflow
description:
## Summary

- Moves GPU test infrastructure from running everything on self-hosted GPU runners to a two-stage Docker-based approach
- **Build stage** (`build-gpu-image`): On a cheap GitHub-hosted runner, builds a Docker image with R (via rig), all dependencies, torch (with tests), LibTorch, and cudatoolkit pre-installed. Pushes to ghcr.io.
- **Test stage** (`test-gpu`, `test-cudatoolkit`): On the GPU runner, pulls the pre-built image and only runs `testthat::test_package('torch')` — no compilation, no dependency installation
- Removes the GPU matrix entry and `check-cudatoolkit` job from the existing `check` workflow
- The `check` job for macOS, Windows, and Linux CPU is unchanged

This should significantly reduce GPU runner wall time since the expensive build/install work now happens on GitHub-hosted runners.

## Test plan

## Changes in this release
- **Breaking**: LibTorch 2.8.0 update, 1-based indexing for `torch_triu_indices()`, `torch_tril_indices()`, and `$indices()`
- **New features**: `torch_sitrep()`, `%*%` operator, `head()`/`tail()` for tensors, exported `torch_scaled_dot_product_attention()`, `torch_sparse_sampled_addmm()`, `torch_ldexp()`, cudatoolkit integration, improved sparse tensor support
- **Bug fixes**: sparse CSR tensors, `bfloat16` dtype, R longjump exceptions, R 4.6 compatibility, and more

title: Fix CRAN check: replace non-API R_UnboundValue
description:
## Summary

- Removes references to `R_UnboundValue` (a non-API R symbol) from code compiled on R >= 4.5.0
- Uses `R_MissingArg` as the sentinel value for `R_getVarEx()` instead
- On R < 4.5.0, converts `R_UnboundValue` from `Rf_findVarInFrame()` to `R_MissingArg` immediately, so `dots_size()` only checks `R_MissingArg`

Fixes CRAN notes:
```
Found non-API call to R: 'R_UnboundValue'
Compiled code should not call non-API entry points in R.
```

## Test plan
- [ ] `R CMD check` passes without the non-API note
- [ ] Tensor indexing (`x[1, ]`, `x[, 1]`, `x[]`, etc.) still works correctly

title: Integrate cudatoolkit R package for CUDA library loading
description:
## Summary

- Adds `load_cudatoolkit_libs()` in `R/lantern_load.R` that detects an installed `cuda*` R package (e.g. `cuda12.8`) and preloads its shared libraries via `dyn.load(local = FALSE, now = FALSE)` before lantern initialization. This makes CUDA symbols globally available so libtorch can resolve them without a system-wide CUDA toolkit installation.
- Adds a `check-cudatoolkit` CI job that runs on a `nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-base-ubuntu22.04` container (driver libs only, no CUDA toolkit), installs `cuda12.8` from r-universe, and runs the full test suite with `TORCH_TEST_CUDA=1`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `check-cudatoolkit` CI job passes: torch loads CUDA from the `cuda12.8` R package
- [ ] Existing CI jobs are unaffected (`load_cudatoolkit_libs()` is a no-op when no cudatoolkit package is installed)
- [ ] CPU-only installations continue to work (function short-circuits when `CUDA` is unset or `"cpu"`)

title: Fix sparse CSR tensor bugs: print, to_sparse, as_array
description:
## Summary

Fixes #1429 — three bugs with CSR sparse tensor support:

- **Print crash**: Printing a CSR tensor threw "Sparse CSR tensors do not have is_contiguous" because LibTorch's `operator<<` calls `is_contiguous()`. Fixed by converting compressed sparse tensors to dense before printing in `_lantern_Tensor_StreamInsertion`.

- **`$to_sparse()` segfault**: Calling `$to_sparse()` on a CSR tensor crashed R with a segfault due to a type mismatch — the Rcpp layer passes a raw `torch::Layout*` but the Lantern layer interprets it as `self_contained::optional::Layout*`. Added an R-level override that routes through the `sparse_dim` overload, avoiding the broken layout code path. The underlying C++ type mismatch for `from_raw::optional::Layout` should be addressed separately in the headers project.

- **`as_array()` didn't catch CSR tensors**: `is_sparse()` only returns TRUE for COO format. Added `is_sparse_csr()` method (covers CSR, CSC, BSR, BSC) and updated `as_array` to check both sparse formats.

Also adds layout constants and string representations for all compressed sparse formats (CSR, CSC, BSR, BSC).

## Test plan

- [x] CSR sparse tensors print without error
- [x] `is_sparse_csr()` returns correct results for dense, CSR, and COO tensors
- [x] `$to_sparse()` converts CSR back to COO without crashing
- [x] `$to_sparse(sparse_dim = 2L)` works correctly
- [x] `as_array()` gives a helpful error for CSR sparse tensors

title: fix: remove redundant lantern.h include causing macro redefinition warning
description:
## Summary
- Removes the redundant `#include <lantern/lantern.h>` from `device.cpp`, which was the only source file with this extra include
- `torch.h` already includes `lantern/lantern.h` with the correct `LANTERN_API` weak linkage definition; the earlier direct include defined `LANTERN_API` as empty, then `torch.h` redefined it as `__attribute__((weak))`, triggering `-Wmacro-redefined`

## Test plan
- [x] Verified `pkgbuild::compile_dll()` compiles `device.cpp` with no warnings
- [x] Confirmed the warning was present before the fix and absent after

title: Bump actions/download-artifact from 7 to 8
description:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 7 to 8.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

title: Bump to libtorch 2.8.0
description:
## Summary

- Update libtorch from 2.7.1 to 2.8.0
- Generate Declarations-2.8.0.yaml from PyTorch v2.8.0 source
- Fix Linux download URL format (2.8.0 dropped `cxx11-abi` from filenames)
- Update lantern CMakeLists.txt to match

## Why 2.8.0?

PyTorch 2.8 introduced the **stable libtorch ABI**, which means code compiled against 2.8 can link with 2.9, 2.10, etc. without recompiling. This is a good foundation for future upgrades.

## API Changes

No breaking changes. Only 3 new functions added:
- `_fused_rms_norm`
- `_weight_int4pack_mm_with_scales_and_zeros`
- `_grouped_mm`

## Testing

Built and tested locally on Ubuntu 24.04 with CUDA 12.8. Basic tensor operations and matmul chains work correctly.

## Notes

This PR includes the code changes but lantern binaries would need to be rebuilt against libtorch 2.8.0 and uploaded to the CDN.

Happy to help with any adjustments needed.

title: fix: dataset/nn_module crash when initialize parameter is named 'd'
description:
Fixes #1336
Using `d` as a parameter name in `initialize` caused an "attempt to apply non-function" error in dataset(), nn_module(), and other class factories.

The internal create_class() function stored the R6 class in a local variable also named `d`. When the user's initialize had a `d` parameter, it shadowed that variable inside the generated wrapper, so `d$new()` tried to call the user's argument as a function instead of the R6 class.

Fix: renamed the internal variable to `.__class__` to avoid any clash with user-defined parameter names.

title: Export torch_sparse_sampled_addmm function
description:
## Summary
- Export `torch_sparse_sampled_addmm()` which was already fully implemented at the C++/Rcpp layer but not exported or documented.
- Add roxygen2 documentation with description, parameter docs, and a runnable example.

The function performs a **Sampled Dense-Dense Matrix Multiplication (SDDMM)**: it computes the matrix product of two dense matrices, but only at the non-zero positions of a sparse CSR mask tensor. This avoids materializing the full dense result, which is critical for memory-efficient operations on large sparse datasets.

Closes #1425

## Test plan
- [x] Verified `torch_sparse_sampled_addmm()` executes correctly with sparse CSR input and returns expected results
- [ ] R CMD check passes

title: Replace Rf_findVarInFrame with R_getVarEx for R 4.6 compatibility
description:
## Summary
- Replace non-API entry point `Rf_findVarInFrame` with the documented replacement `R_getVarEx` in `src/indexing.cpp`
- Uses `R_getVarEx(R_DotsSymbol, env, FALSE, R_UnboundValue)` which preserves identical behavior (returns `R_UnboundValue` when variable not found)
- Guarded with `#if R_VERSION >= R_Version(4, 5, 0)` for backwards compatibility with older R versions
- `R_MissingArg` and `R_UnboundValue` are kept as-is — no replacements available yet, and rlang follows the same approach (r-lib/rlang#1889)

## Context
CRAN NOTEs about calls to `Rf_findVarInFrame` will soon become WARNINGs, and the entry point will be removed in R 4.6.0 (late April 2026). See "Some API replacements for non-API entry points" in Writing R Extensions.

title: Export torch_scaled_dot_product_attention
description:
`torch_scaled_dot_product_attention` was implemented but not exported, forcing users to access it via `get(..., envir = asNamespace("torch"))`. This prevented straightforward use of the fused CUDA kernels that provide 2-3x speedup over manual attention computation.

## Changes

- **R/gen-namespace-docs.R**: Added roxygen documentation with `@export` tag covering all 8 parameters, mathematical formula, and examples for basic usage, causal masking, and custom attention masks
- **NAMESPACE**: Added export declaration
- **tests/testthat/test-gen-namespace.R**: Added tests for basic usage, causal masking, attention masks, and dropout

## Usage

```r
library(torch)

query <- torch_randn(2, 8, 10, 64)  # (batch, heads, seq_len, dim)
key <- torch_randn(2, 8, 10, 64)
value <- torch_randn(2, 8, 10, 64)

# Now accessible directly
output <- torch_scaled_dot_product_attention(query, key, value)

# Supports causal masking for autoregressive models
output <- torch_scaled_dot_product_attention(query, key, value, is_causal = TRUE)
```

title: Exclude glibc libraries from dependency bundling
description:
## Summary

Excludes glibc libraries from the `RUNTIME_DEPENDENCY_SET` to prevent bundling system libraries that cause ABI conflicts on newer Linux distributions.

## Problem

The current build bundles glibc 2.31 components from the Ubuntu 20.04 build environment:
- `libc-2.31.so`, `libdl-2.31.so`, `libpthread-2.31.so`, `librt-2.31.so`, `libm-2.31.so`, `ld-2.31.so`

When loaded on systems with newer glibc (e.g., Ubuntu 24.04 with glibc 2.39), `GLIBC_PRIVATE` symbol mismatches cause runtime failures:

```
liblantern.so - libdl.so.2: undefined symbol: _dl_catch_error, version GLIBC_PRIVATE
```

This manifests inconsistently depending on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` ordering - if system library paths come first, system glibc wins and it works; otherwise the bundled glibc 2.31 gets loaded via `liblantern.so`'s `RUNPATH=$ORIGIN` and fails.

## Solution

Add `PRE_EXCLUDE_REGEXES` and `POST_EXCLUDE_REGEXES` to the `install(RUNTIME_DEPENDENCY_SET ...)` command to filter out:
- glibc library names (`libc`, `libdl`, `libpthread`, `librt`, `libm`, `ld-linux`)
- System library paths (`/lib/`, `/lib64/`, `/usr/lib/`)

glibc libraries should **never** be bundled on Linux - they must come from the host system. This is standard practice for portable Linux binaries (cf. manylinux approach).

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify lantern builds successfully with `BUNDLE_DEPENDENCIES=ON`
- [ ] Confirm glibc libraries are not present in the resulting package
- [ ] Test on Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39) with various `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` configurations

## Related issues

- #1323 (Alpine Linux glibc compatibility)
- #663 (ld.so inconsistency)

title: Bump actions/download-artifact from 4 to 5
description:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 4 to 5.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v5.0.0

What's Changed

  • Update README.md by @​nebuk89 in actions/download-artifact#407
  • BREAKING fix: inconsistent path behavior for single artifact downloads by ID by @​GrantBirki in actions/download-artifact#416

v5.0.0

🚨 Breaking Change

This release fixes an inconsistency in path behavior for single artifact downloads by ID. If you're downloading single artifacts by ID, the output path may change.

What Changed

Previously, single artifact downloads behaved differently depending on how you specified the artifact:

  • By name: name: my-artifact → extracted to path/ (direct)
  • By ID: artifact-ids: 12345 → extracted to path/my-artifact/ (nested)

Now both methods are consistent:

  • By name: name: my-artifact → extracted to path/ (unchanged)
  • By ID: artifact-ids: 12345 → extracted to path/ (fixed - now direct)

Migration Guide

✅ No Action Needed If:
  • You download artifacts by name
  • You download multiple artifacts by ID
  • You already use merge-multiple: true as a workaround
⚠️ Action Required If:

You download single artifacts by ID and your workflows expect the nested directory structure.

Before v5 (nested structure):

- uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
  with:
    artifact-ids: 12345
    path: dist
# Files were in: dist/my-artifact/

Where my-artifact is the name of the artifact you previously uploaded

title: Libtorch v2.7.1
description:
Updates for LibTorch v2.7.1

On Ci when running CUDA 12.8 we see:

```
CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device
CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
For debugging consider passing CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
```

This is likely because the our GPU NVIDIA 1080Ti uses Pascal architecture (6.1) and that's now not supported in 12.8. See:

```
TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="5.0;6.0;7.0;7.5;8.0;8.6"
case ${CUDA_VERSION} in
    12.8)
        TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.5;8.0;8.6;9.0;10.0;12.0+PTX" #removing sm_50-sm_70 as these architectures are deprecated in CUDA 12.8 and will be removed in future releases
        EXTRA_CAFFE2_CMAKE_FLAGS+=("-DATEN_NO_TEST=ON")
        ;;
    12.6)
        TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="${TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST};9.0"
        EXTRA_CAFFE2_CMAKE_FLAGS+=("-DATEN_NO_TEST=ON")
        ;;
    12.4)
        TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="${TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST};9.0"
        EXTRA_CAFFE2_CMAKE_FLAGS+=("-DATEN_NO_TEST=ON")
        ;;
    11.8)
        TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="${TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST};3.7;9.0"
        EXTRA_CAFFE2_CMAKE_FLAGS+=("-DATEN_NO_TEST=ON")
        ;;
    *)
        echo "unknown cuda version $CUDA_VERSION"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
```

[in the repo](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/e2d141dbde55c2a4370fac5165b0561b6af4798b/.ci/manywheel/build_cuda.sh#L54-L71)

Thus CI now uses 12.6. Looking forward we'll need to upgrade our runner GPU or move to using a different CI runner.

title: Change default installation path to R's cache directory.
description:
We used to check if the R's library where the package has been installed is writable and in that case install torch into that library. However, CRAN is no longer allowing us even to check if this directory is writable during checks. 

With this PR we'll default to installing torch to the cache directory. The drawback of this approach is that I don't think this directory is cleaned up when a package is removed. It's shared between R versions too. 

It's thus possible that with time this directory becomes full of LibTorch and LibLantern installations.
Users can clean it up using `torch::torch_cache_dir_purge()`.

title: fix R-level fr-FR translation
description:
After some exchange with Philippe Grosjean during the French Rencontre R 2024, 
I finally got the correct way to wrap R-level messages so that they get translated.

```{r}
> withr::with_language(lang = "fr",
+                      torch_scalar_tensor(torch_randn(8, 2, 7))
+ )
Error in `value_error()` at torch/R/creation-ops.R:380:5:
! les valeurs doivent être de longueur 1
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.
Called from: signal_abort(cnd, .file)
Browse[1]> 
> 
```

**Note**
Cpp-level translation is 
 - missing (no collection of the messages in po(t) files yet) 
 - not working as it requires wrapping all C/C++ level `"messages"` into `_("message")` but gettext does not get the one in `Rcpp::stop()`. I'll make it explicit in a issue.

title: feat: nn-transformer module
description:
Hi everyone,

I've had a go at adding the `TransformerEncoderLayer` and `TransformerEncoder` modules from PyTorch, hoping to eventually address issue #1209. I'm opening this as a draft PR because the R torch codebase is really new to me, and I suspect there are many aspects of my implementation that are wrong, could be improved or adjusted, and I am hoping that this may be helpful for others to help with as well (if not please ignore). 

In particular, I'd really appreciate guidance on the following:

- C++: I am just a bit lost here about how to start to bring across the cpp for this (similar to https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/transformer.cpp?) into the R torch (tried looking at rnn to get my bearings but struggling) so I have not tried yet. 

- Testing: Are the provided tests helpful and sufficient, or is there anything critical that's missing? I'm not sure if I've covered all edge cases or if additional tests would be beneficial but have checked coverage is 100% against the new `nn-transfer.R`

- Code structure: I've tried to follow existing conventions, which I based on comparing how `nn-rnn` module was developed in relation to PyTorch equivalent but I'd appreciate any pointers if things are structured incorrectly or could be more idiomatic.

- Argument checks and defaults: Have I included enough checks on the provided arguments? Are the defaults sensible, or is anything critical missing? (PyTorch has significantly more but was basing on `nn-rnn`). 

My plan, once this initial PR is in better shape, is to add the `TransformerDecoderLayer` and then the full `Transformer` module, and then if I can figure it out or if someone else can help with adding the cpp for this. Before proceeding further, it would be really helpful to have your feedback and pointers to see if I’m at all on the right track.

Thanks very much in advance and hopefully this is helpful. 

All the best,

OJ

title: Add spam dataset from Elements of Statistical Learning
description:
# Add spam_dataset from Elements of Statistical Learning (GSoC-25 tasks)

## Description
This PR adds a new dataset implementation for the spam email classification dataset from the "Elements of Statistical Learning" book. This dataset contains 4601 emails with 57 features and a binary classification indicating whether the email is spam or not.

## Features
- Implementation of `spam_dataset()` function with documentation
- Test suite to verify dataset functionality
- Example vignette showing how to use the dataset for a classification task

## Use Case
This dataset can be useful for binary classification exercises and demos, as it's a well-known dataset in the statistical learning community. It's relatively small (compared to image datasets) but provides a realistic classification problem.

## Testing
- All tests for the new dataset pass
- Manual verification of the dataset loader and example usage has been performed

title: Add CUDA memory snapshot to help debug CUDA memory use
description:
Implemented bindings for LibTorch `_record_memory_history` and `_memory_snapshot_pickled`, similar to the python implementation: [https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/torch_cuda_memory.html](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/torch_cuda_memory.html).

The created memory snapshots can be uploaded to [https://pytorch.org/memory_viz](https://pytorch.org/memory_viz) and used to debug CUDA OOM errors, see blog posts: [https://pytorch.org/blog/understanding-gpu-memory-1/](https://pytorch.org/blog/understanding-gpu-memory-1/) and [https://pytorch.org/blog/understanding-gpu-memory-2/](https://pytorch.org/blog/understanding-gpu-memory-2/).

Included minor details in the memory management vignette, which seemed like a logical place to outline the feature.

title: fix(ignite): making state saveable, param_groups modifieable
description:
It was impossible to save the state because of:

* https://github.com/mlverse/torch/issues/1233
* undefined tensors were part of the state such as max_exp_avg_sq for adam with amsgrad = FALSE. We now keep them as 0-sized tensors as undefined tensors are not serializeable. (The reason we keep them at all is that it simplifies the saving and loading of state dicts easier)

This PR also improves the tests by removing an unnecessary call to `torch_manual_seed()` that made the tests deterministic

Fix/trace mode
description:
Bugfixes:
* save-load roundtrip used to convert `script_function` into `script_module`. This is fixed now (in a somewhat hacky way)

Open questions.
* In this PR, we only do the train-eval distinction for the `$forward` method. Maybe we want to do this for all methods.
* Can we register the `$forward` method (that distinguishes between the internal train and eval forward method) in the underlying script module instead of the `nn_Module`?
* Reading a script function is currently loaded as a module, I don't think this should be the case

TODOs:
* [ ] the training mode after saving a `script_module` is changed. This should probably be fixed.
* [ ] Currently, after saving a trace-jitted module, the `$forward` method is not defined. This is because the underlying module class is not saved when saving a trace jitted module, so when loading it again, the unpatched methods are used.
* [ ] Properly distinguish between saved module and saved function. The current hack does not work for jitted modules that were saved with an old version.

title: Add a currently unexported `torch_tensor_free` that deletes tensors without requiring us to wait for GC.
description:
@sebffischer Do you want to try out and see if this allows some speedups on your setup?
I didn't see speedups on MPS (memory management on mps is soo different), but maybe it helps with CUDA:

```
library(torch)

p = 100
steps = 1000
n = 1000

device = "mps"

X = torch_randn(n, p, device = device)
beta = torch_randn(p, 1, device = device)
Y = X$matmul(beta)

latent = 5000

net = nn_sequential(
  nn_linear(p, latent),
  nn_relu(),
  nn_linear(latent, 1)
)

net$to(device = device)
opt = optim_adam(net$parameters, lr = 0.01)

t1 = Sys.time()

for (i in 1:steps) {
  opt$zero_grad()
  Y_hat = net(X)
  loss = nnf_mse_loss(Y, Y_hat)
  loss$backward()
  torch:::torch_tensor_free(loss)
  torch:::torch_tensor_free(Y_hat)
}

t2 = Sys.time()

print(paste0("Total time: ", t2 - t1))
```

title: New serialization
description:
This PR will add a new serialization version based on safetensors.

The new serialization version is a safetensor file containing the `state_dict` (ie tensors in the R object) concatenated with a `serialize()`d version of the R object.

This has a few advantages:

- It's much faster as we need much less copies of tensors in order to serialize.
- It's interoperable, since the first part of the file is a bare safetensors file, you can read the tensors in the file using any implementation of safetensors.
- It's ready to write directly into a connection, thus we won't need to first write to a raw vector, then write to the connection.

We won't break the older serialization version. It will still be accessible by setting the serialization version option.

TODO:

- [x] Add support for more types of tensors. We should fallback to the legacy serialization when we find an unsupported data type.
- [x] Keep the `requires_grad` attribute correctly.

Bench:

```
# A tibble: 2 × 13
  expression      min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec` n_itr  n_gc total_time result memory     time      
  <bch:expr> <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl> <int> <dbl>   <bch:tm> <list> <list>     <list>    
1 v3             55ms   58.7ms     16.9     10.8MB     1.88     9     1      532ms <NULL> <Rprofmem> <bench_tm>
2 v2            377ms  377.2ms      2.65      59MB     2.65     2     2      754ms <NULL> <Rprofmem> <bench_tm>
# ℹ 1 more variable: gc <list>
```

This results in a 30% speedup with parallel datalaoders too: 

<details>
<summary>Code</summary>

```
library(torch)

batch_size <- as.numeric(Sys.getenv("BATCH_SIZE", unset = "1000"))
device <- Sys.getenv("DEVICE", unset = "cpu")

Dataset <- dataset(
  initialize = function(ir, batch_size) {
    self$len <- ir*batch_size
    self$batch_size <- batch_size
  },
  .getbatch = function(i) {
    list(
      torch_randn(self$batch_size, 28, 28),
      torch_randint(1, 10, size = c(self$batch_size))
    )
  },
  .length = function() {
    self$len
  }
)

fn <- function() {
  coro::loop(for(el in dataloader(ds, batch_size = batch_size, num_workers = 4)) {
    x <- el[[1]]
    y <- el[[2]]
  })
  invisible(NULL)
}

iter <- 1
ds <- Dataset(iter, batch_size)

fn()

iter <- as.numeric(Sys.getenv("ITER", unset = "1000"))
ds <- Dataset(iter, batch_size)

cat(system.time(fn())[["elapsed"]])
```
</details>

```
set.seed(777)
torch_manual_seed(777)
train_data <- list(torch_arange(1, 100)$unsqueeze(2), 2 * torch_arange(1, 100)$unsqueeze(2))

At this point, it looks like just removing the interim conversions to R is enough; but I'll try further initializations.

The motivation behind this module is that it is used by wav2vec2 model and without it, the parameter names do not match (weight_v, weight_g).  I'm trying to port it to torchaudio ([branch in devel here](https://github.com/Athospd/torchaudio/tree/wav2vec2)).

Some caveats:
- not tested in gpu
- The original implementation uses hooks to perform a pre-forward operation. I had to adapt the code since R torch still do not support hooks.

Thank you

description:
Hi Daniel,

can you please take a look at this?
It successfully exports the function, but I was not sure how to handle the keyword arguments (I think they're subsumed under `TensorOptions`, but still, documented as usual?).

Also, `document.R` [still ]behaves weirdly for me; always crashes on first execution. Do you have that too?

Finally, I've gotten `.Rd` files (which have not been added [yet]), which do three different kinds of things:

1) add back the "if torch installed" line. I guess this one is removed when not using `document.R`?

2) remove this (in `linalg_cond.R`):

```
-\tabular{ll}{
-   \code{p} \tab matrix norm \cr
-   \code{NULL} \tab \code{2}-norm (largest singular value) \cr
-   \code{'fro'} \tab Frobenius norm \cr
-   \code{'nuc'} \tab nuclear norm \cr
-   \code{Inf} \tab \code{max(sum(abs(x), dim=2))} \cr
-   \code{-Inf} \tab \code{min(sum(abs(x), dim=2))} \cr
-   \code{1} \tab \code{max(sum(abs(x), dim=1))} \cr
-   \code{-1} \tab \code{min(sum(abs(x), dim=1))} \cr
-   \code{2} \tab largest singular value \cr
-   \code{-2} \tab smallest singular value \cr
-}
```

3) remove this (in various optimizer files)

```
-\section{Warning}{
-If you need to move a model to GPU via \verb{$cuda()}, please do so before
-constructing optimizers for it. Parameters of a model after \verb{$cuda()}
-will be different objects from those before the call. In general, you
-should make sure that the objects pointed to by model parameters subject
-to optimization remain the same over the whole lifecycle of optimizer
-creation and usage.
-}
```


Should I add these files? 

Also, I see we point to `document.R` in the contributing guide. However, perhaps visibility would be better if this was made part of the previous section (workflow)?

Thanks!

title: Call `gc` with different configs
description:
Call full `gc` when out of memory so we can achieve better memory usage.

I couldn't find a way to synchronously call GC while in a backward call (see https://discuss.pytorch.org/t/deadlock-when-freeing-memory/154102 ). So the way we are solving this is by always calling GC before backward and by calling GC asynchronously when more memory is requested, in the hope that memory is release before the OOM error.

title: terminate called without an active exception
description:
Fixes intermittent crash when quitting the R session causing by scheduling desynchronization.
Depending on the order this would be called:

https://github.com/mlverse/torch/blob/720a546f71e7a4d2765c550d6e5fd67b874f5d39/src/autograd.cpp#L69-L73

and the event loop stops. The thread would never be joined. This would cause a crash when exiting the R session because unjoined/undetached threads can cause problems.

We solved by having a special finalization tasks, that are called right before exiting the event loop.

title: Feature/prune head
description:
fix #812 

I've a few test that pass on mlverse packages and friends, but I'm not sure if {torch} is the right location to host them. I include them for reference (and or later on dispatch) 
## {tochvision} model pruning 

```{r}
test_that("we can prune head of torchvision resnet34 moels", {
  resnet34 <- model_resnet34(pretrained=TRUE)

  expect_error(prune <- nn_prune_head(resnet34, 1), NA)
  # expect_true(inherits(prune, "nn_sequential"))
  expect_equal(length(prune), 9)
  expect_true(inherits(prune[[length(prune)]], "nn_adaptive_avg_pool2d"))
  
  input <- torch::torch_randn(1, 3, 256, 256)
  out <- prune(input)
  expect_tensor_shape(out, c(1, 512, 1, 1))

})

test_that("we can prune head of torchvision resnet50 moels", {
  resnet50 <- model_resnet50(pretrained=TRUE)

  expect_error(prune <- nn_prune_head(resnet50, 1), NA)
  expect_true(inherits(prune, "nn_sequential"))
  expect_equal(length(prune), 9)
  expect_true(inherits(prune[[length(prune)]], "nn_adaptive_avg_pool2d"))
    
  input <- torch::torch_randn(1, 3, 256, 256)
  out <- prune(input)
  expect_tensor_shape(out, c(1, 2048, 1, 1))


})

test_that("we can prune head of torchvision resnext101 moels", {
  resnext101 <- model_resnext101_32x8d(pretrained=TRUE)

  expect_error(prune <- torch:::nn_prune_head(resnext101, 1), NA)
  expect_true(inherits(prune, "nn_sequential"))
  expect_equal(length(prune), 9)
  expect_true(inherits(prune[[length(prune)]], "nn_adaptive_avg_pool2d"))
    
  input <- torch::torch_randn(1, 3, 256, 256)
  out <- prune(input)
  expect_tensor_shape(out, c(1, 2048, 1, 1))


})
test_that("we can prune head of torchvision mobilenetv2 moels", {
  mobilenet <- model_mobilenet_v2(pretrained=TRUE)

  expect_error(prune <- nn_prune_head(mobilenet, 1), NA)
  expect_true(inherits(prune, "nn_sequential"))
  expect_equal(length(prune), 1)
  expect_true(inherits(prune[[length(prune)]], "nn_sequential"))
    
  input <- torch::torch_randn(1, 3, 256, 256)
  out <- prune(input)
  expect_tensor_shape(out, c(1, 1280, 8, 8))
})
```
## {torchaudio} model pruning

```{r}
test_that("we can prune head of torchaudio melresnet models", {
  melresnet  <-  model_melresnet()
  
  expect_error(prune <- torch:::nn_prune_head(melresnet[[1]], 1), NA)
  expect_true(inherits(prune, "nn_sequential"))
  # expect_equal(length(prune), 9)
  expect_true(inherits(prune[[length(prune)]], "ResBlock"))
  
  input  <-  torch::torch_rand(10, 128, 512)  
  output  <-  prune(input)  # shape: (10, 128, 508)
  expect_tensor_shape(output, c(10, 128, 508))
})  
```
# {torchtransformer} model pruning
```{r}
emb_size <- 128L
mpe <- 512L
n_head <- 4L
n_layer <- 6L
vocab_size <- 30522L
n_inputs <- 2
n_token_max <- 128L
t_ids <- matrix(
  sample(
    2:vocab_size,
    size = n_token_max * n_inputs,
    replace = TRUE
  ),
  nrow = n_token_max, ncol = n_inputs
)
ttype_ids <- matrix(
  rep(1L, n_token_max * n_inputs),
  nrow = n_token_max, ncol = n_inputs
)

test_that("we can prune head of torchtransformer  model", {
  model <- model_bert(
    embedding_size = emb_size,
    n_layer = n_layer,
    n_head = n_head,
    max_position_embeddings = mpe,
    vocab_size = vocab_size
  )
  expect_error(prune <- nn_prune_head(model), NA)
  output  <-  prune(
    torch::torch_tensor(t_ids),
    torch::torch_tensor(ttype_ids)
    
)
  expect_tensor_shape(output, c(128, 2, 128))

})
```

title: Dataloaders with socket conection
description:
Passing data between the workers can now be accelerated by using socket connections.
```
> bench_ds <- dataset(
+   initialize = function(size_of_tensor) {
+     self$size_of_tensor <- size_of_tensor
+   },
+   .getitem = function(i) {
+     list(x = torch_randn(self$size_of_tensor))
+   },
+   .length = function() {32*20}
+ )
> system.time({
+   withr::with_options(list(torch.dataloader_use_socket_con = TRUE), {
+     dl <- dataloader(bench_ds(256*256*3), batch_size = 32, num_workers = 4)
+     coro::loop(for(x in dl) {
+       k <- x
+     })
+   })
+ })
   user  system elapsed 
 48.416   2.419  58.796 
> system.time({
+   withr::with_options(list(torch.dataloader_use_socket_con = FALSE), {
+     dl <- dataloader(bench_ds(256*256*3), batch_size = 32, num_workers = 4)
+     coro::loop(for(x in dl) {
+       k <- x
+     })
+   })
+ })
   user  system elapsed 
 61.417   2.273  74.165 
```

Next steps should be investing in `torch_save` speedups, specially, if we could avoid the compression.
Perhaps, also finding a different way of serializing the tensor.

title: On Windows query cuda_version from nvcc instead from version.txt
description:
Hi, this PR solves the issue #797 on windows that the `version.txt` file is not present anymore from CUDA 11 onwards. It now uses the same function as already is used on Linux to query the `cuda_version` from the nvcc command instead of parsing `version.txt`. However, instead of the using environment variable `CUDA_HOME`  (which is used on linux) `CUDA_PATH` is used and it refers to the nvcc executable.

Testing it on my windows machine with CUDA 11.1 resulted in a successful installation of `torch` for gpu.

title: Make dataloaders slightly faster by using a custom transpose function.
description:
The new function used for transposing the batches when 'collating' in the dataloader is ~6x. This makes dataloader in general slightly faster ~3/4% in a typical example.

``` r
library(purrr)
library(collapse)
#> Warning: package 'collapse' was built under R version 4.1.2
#> collapse 1.7.5, see ?`collapse-package` or ?`collapse-documentation`
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'collapse'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     D

batch <- purrr::rerun(1000, x = array(1, c(32,32,3)), y = runif(5))
transpose2 <- torch:::transpose2

bench::mark(
  old = lapply(setNames(1:2, names(batch[[1]])), function(i) {
    lapply(batch, function(x) x[[i]])
  }),
  new = transpose2(batch),
  purrr = transpose(batch),
  base = do.call(Map, c(f = list, batch)),
  collapase = t_list(batch)
)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   expression      min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr> <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 old           928µs   1.02ms      966.      94KB     51.8
#> 2 new           123µs 139.42µs     6958.    18.2KB     44.3
#> 3 purrr         205µs 226.97µs     4301.    18.1KB     52.4
#> 4 base          822µs 927.39µs     1034.    70.8KB     50.0
#> 5 collapase     291µs 331.25µs     2941.    40.9KB     21.3
```

title: Refactor internal lantern types
description:
We want to get rid of `LanternObject` in favor of constructors `from_raw` and `make_unique`. Users building extensions won't need to understand implementation details like 'what's LanternObject vs LanternPtr', handling of optionals and etc.

Missing handling - possibly others too:

- [x] `LanternObject<std::array<bool,3>`
- [x] `LanternObject<std::array<bool,4>`
- [x] `LanternObject<std::array<bool,2>>`
- [x]  `LanternObject<c10::optional<std::string>>`
- [x] `LanternObject<c10::optional<torch::MemoryFormat>>`
- [x] `LanternObject<c10::optional<torch::IntArrayRef>>`
- [x] `LanternObject<c10::optional<torch::Scalar>>`
- [x] `LanternObject<torch::ArrayRef<torch::Scalar>>`
- [x] `LanternObject<c10::optional<torch::ArrayRef<double>>>`
- [x] `LanternObject<c10::List<c10::optional<torch::Tensor>>>`
- [x]  `at::Stream`
- [x] Remove `LanternObject` usages from deleters and factory of raw pointers.
- [ ] Think about an unified Object type that knows about it's type and it's deleter. This would allow us to make 'deleting' completely transparent to the Rcpp layer. Allowing for a much smaller namespace in that side. Also allow simplifying a lot of the `XPtrTorch` subclasses.

Decided to leave this last work item for the future. The current front-end API seems fine and all this other changes can be made in the future without breaking code.

title: Prepare v0.6.1 release
description:
Fix required version of knitr because 1.35 is ignoring the global chunk options.

CRAN requested a re-submission to fix valgrind errors. Turns out the valgrind errors are false positives and they only happen because vignettes should not be evaluated on CRAN, however knitr 1.35 seems to be ignoring the global chunk options that we set to prevent evaluation.

This release is simply going to pin a minimum `knitr` required version so CRAN doesn't run the vignettes.
THe check log is available here: https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/bdr/memtests/valgrind/torch/00check.log

and here's an excerpt of the problem:

```
> knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", 
+     eval = identical(Sys.getenv("TORCH_TEST", unset = "0"), "1"))

> library(torch)

> torch_manual_seed(1)
==302325== Jump to the invalid address stated on the next line
==302325==    at 0x0: ???
==302325==    by 0x5: ???
==302325==  Address 0x0 is not stack'd, malloc'd or (recently) free'd
==302325== 

 *** caught segfault ***
address (nil), cause 'invalid permissions'
```

title: Better handle tensor identity
description:
Save a weak reference to the tensor R XPtr inside the TensorImpl, this allows us to return the same XPtr when this field is set, making it easier to track tensors identity. Because now this is as simple as comparing if both xptrs are the same or not.

This same idea is used by PyTorch and learned about it after listening to the incredible Pytorch Dev podcast. Specifically the [history and constraints of tensor episode](https://pytorch-dev-podcast.simplecast.com/episodes/history-and-constraints-of-tensor).

The tricky part here was that even though we registered a callback that would delete the weak reference from TensorImpl when the XPtr goes out of scope, there was no guarantee that this was called before a new reference was requested. However, R could have already scheduled it for deletion so we ended up with a XPtr pointing to an object that was already deleted. Calling `R_RunPendingFinalizers()` fixed this problem.

This PR was intended only to fix #564 but turned out to be more complex becuase there was no way yo pass optional tensors to `at::diff` from R because they were automatically converted to `undefined` tensors.

Most libtorch's api handles undefined tensors and optional tenors as the same thing, but this is not always true. They seem to be laing towards a declarative optional approach - see: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/51456 

Thus this PR, also changes the calls that used `undefined` tensors to specify optional parameters to a declarative approach by introducing the `XPtrTorchOptionalTensor` class in the Rcpp side.

title: Unwrapping arguments passed from R
description:
Allows unwrapping arguments from R without using autogenerated code.

This will eventually allow us to remove the `argument_to_torch` function that is the main overhead when calling torch functions. 

https://github.com/mlverse/torch/blob/480a0113347d4d9f369e231761f3180c8928c173/R/codegen-utils.R#L34-L169


TODO:

* [x] int64_t index autocastiing
* [x] IndexTensorList autocasting
* [x] remove all other transformation of `obj` in `argument_to_torch_type`.

This allows us to gain some speedups, specially with small models where the R overhead can be significatnly larger. 

A simple benchmark gives us 37% speedup for small ops:

```
x <- torch_randn(10, 10)
w <- torch_randn(10, 10)

bench::mark(
  a = torch_mm(x, w)
)
```

CRAN torch:

```
# A tibble: 1 x 13
  expression     min  median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec` n_itr  n_gc total_time result memory time  gc   
  <bch:expr> <bch:t> <bch:t>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl> <int> <dbl>   <bch:tm> <list> <list> <lis> <lis>
1 a           54.6µs  62.9µs    14855.    19.9KB     14.8  7016     7      472ms <trch… <Rpro… <bch… <tib…
```

This PR:

```
# A tibble: 1 x 13
  expression     min  median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec` n_itr  n_gc total_time result memory time  gc   
  <bch:expr> <bch:t> <bch:t>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl> <int> <dbl>   <bch:tm> <list> <list> <lis> <lis>
1 a           35.3µs  39.1µs    23586.    4.98KB     9.44  9996     4      424ms <trch… <Rpro… <bch… <tib…
```

This PR also allows us to rewrite the dispatcher in C++ in the future.

title: Worker globals
description:
This PR introduces 2 new parameters to the `dataloader` function:

- `worker_globals`: objects that should be copied to the global environment of each worker.
- `worker_packages`: names of packages that should be loaded with `library` into each worker.

The code wouldn't work before, because the `hello_fn` wouldn't be available in the workers:

```
ds <- dataset(
    .length = function() {20},
    initialize = function() {},
    .getitem = function(id) {
      hello_fn()
    }
  )
  
dl <- dataloader(ds(), batch_size = 10, num_workers = 2)
```

You can now create the dataloader with:

```
dl <- dataloader(ds(), batch_size = 10, num_workers = 2, worker_globals = list(
    hello_fn = hello_fn
  ))
```

Fix for #444

title: Start experimenting with jit support
description:
The scope of this PR is to implement the equivalent to trace an R function to a ScriptFunction(https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/fa560ceb9c8cd0b7e40c3e7ec7808c01d2399377/torch/csrc/jit/python/script_init.cpp#L1111-L1196) in PyTorch.

- We will only add tracing, ie. loops that depend on data attributes are not supported.
- The script function doesn't act like an nn_module, meaning that you don't train it. However we will be able to save it to a file a load it in python or c++...

Support for ScriptModules is possible but requires implementing a ModuleWrapper (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/fa560ceb9c8cd0b7e40c3e7ec7808c01d2399377/torch/nn/cpp.py#L49)  

TODOS:

- [x] Implement `torch::jit::Stack` <-> R lists. (very basic support implemented)
- [x] Convert the R function to a function taking and returning stacks. (done in the c++ side only)
- [x] Figure out what to return from the traceable fn? The graph or the function created in the compilation unit?
- [x] R functionality to easily create R function taking and returning stacks
- [x] R capsule for the pointer returned by the trace_fn, with possibility to print the graph and etc. Similar to the ScriptFunction
- [x] JIT save and JIT load
- [x] Allow printing the generated graph
- [x] Add tests for more complex functions
- [x] Complete support for most IValues when creating Stacks.
- [x] Allow loading JIT functions (created in python or R)
- [x] Dispose of memory allocated when creating the traceable function.
