title: Rename package back to 'torch'
description:
Fix for https://github.com/mlverse/torch/issues/30.

Currently, `rcpp` does not support naming the library that gets generated, instead it uses `Package` from the `DESCRIPTION` file. So I think we are left with limited options:
1) Send a PR to `rcpp` to include a new `LibName` attribute in the `DESCRIPTION` field.
2) Rename the library ourselves.

This PR goes for (2) as a start, which happens to work fine except that it currently generates two libraries `torch.so` and `torchpkg.so` which increases the size of the package 2x. This is fine during development but we should remove the extra library from being generated when release to CRAN, see comment in [tools/renamelib.R](https://github.com/mlverse/torch/pull/34/files#diff-356a22515ff105ce4f2863f90a0f1613R6).

title: Prepare lantern for long-tail of error handling
description: Appart from autograd and autogen functions, we also need to handle errors across all our custom lantern functions. This PR adds support for a `LANTERN_HOST_HANDLER` define hook, to allow torch to define a custom try/catch across all functions without having to add `LANTERN_ERROR_HANDLES` everywhere in the code.

title: Resolves #164: Implement more R generic methods
description:
This pull request implements the following R generic functions along with the corresponding test cases:
> %%, %/%, &, |, !, abs, sign, sqrt, ceiling, floor, trunc, cumsum, log, log10, log2, log1p, exp, expm1, cos, cosh, sin, sinh, tan, tanh, acos, asin, atan, max, min, prod, sum

While most functions are straightforward to implement, several special cases are noted here:

- `log`: default R has a `base` argument but I didn't find the corresponding in pytorch, so I did a trick as`torch_log(x)/torch_log(base)`
- `sum` and `prod`: `nan`s in the tensor will be ignored if `na.rm=T`. If single tensor is given, one can specify `dim` and `keepdim`. If multiple tensors are given, `dim` argument is not allowed and only a single value will be computed from them.
- `min` and `max`: `nan`s in the tensor will be ignored if `na.rm=T`. Only a single value is returned.

title: Enhance datasets API
description:
In this PR we added a couple of functions to ease iteration of datasets. See examples below:

```
x <- torch_randn(100, 100)
y <- torch_randn(100, 1)
dataset <- utils_dataset_tensor(x, y)
dl <- utils_dataloader(dataset = dataset, batch_size = 32)

# iterating with a while loop
iter <- dataloader_make_iter(dl)
while(!is.null(batch <- dataloader_get_next(iter))) {
   expect_tensor(batch[[1]])
   expect_tensor(batch[[2]])
}
  
# iterating with an enum
for (batch in dataloader_enum(dl)) {
  expect_tensor(batch[[1]])
  expect_tensor(batch[[2]])    
}
```

Thiis fixes #54

Fix for https://github.com/mlverse/torch/issues/90 to avoid re-downloading over-and-over libtorch while doing development. The workflow is to run:

```r
# install torch in home path
Sys.setenv(TORCH_HOME = "~/torch")

# rebuild torch package
# libtorch will be downloaded to TORCH_HOME

# rebuild torch package
# libtorch is found in TORCH_HOME and nothing is downloaded
```

This workflow is not to be used by users, mostly for developers and/or very-advanced users.

title: Refine the API for creation ops
Dataset
description:
This PR implements basic support for `torch.utils.data`.
We are only implementing:

- `Map` style datasets (Iterables are not implemented yet) (fix #42) 
- Single worker Data loaders (fix #43)
- Basic Samplers like batch sampler, random sampler and sequential sampler

Note that we didn't implement any higher lever API, for now the DataLoaders are R6 classes that have an `.iter` method. This method returns a `SingleProcessDataLoaderIter` that includes an `.next` method that can be called to get next batches. We need to think how the API for the datasets will work.

This PR also rewrites the slicing interface to use the [`.index` method of Tensor](https://pytorch.org/cppdocs/notes/tensor_indexing.html) and should be more robust and consistent with pytorch. (fix #45 , fix #46)

This PR also adds a tools/buildlantern.R script that will now be used by the CI to build lantern when checking the R package, so we can easily test how lantern modifications affect the R package. It can also be used when developing to sync lantern and the R package.

title: Register hook
description:
This PR turned out to be more complex than expected.

Since hooks are arbitrary R functions, they must run in the main
thread, but `backward` can call them from other threads..  In order to make sure, 
we call `backward` in a different thread
see `cpp_backward` and leave the main thread free to execute the R
calbacks that are pushed to the `event_loop_thread` as `packaged_tasks` to the `tasks` global.

However, the R hooks can by themselves call `backward` again and torch
does not allow us to use a different thread. so while we are waiting for
the hook to finish, we allow to execute tasks in the thread
the hook has been called.

deleting

CI — New composite action build-rocm-lantern and rocm-kit.yaml workflow handle the libtorch download, build, audit, and artifact upload.

3. add install_torch() option to use it with `Sys.setenv(CUDA="rocm6.4")

###   Change Map

  R/install.R — Adds ROCm detection to the installation chain:
  - is_rocm_version() / check_supported_rocm_version_linux() / rocm_bundle_is_installed() as shared predicates
  - rocm_version_from_system_linux() probes /opt/rocm/.info/version as a fallback in cuda_version()
  - installation_kind() returns the ROCm version string directly
  - cuda_version_from_cudatoolkit() constructs rocmX.Y package names instead of cudarocmX.Y
  - install_torch_sitrep() gains a ROCm/HIP section and guards two CUDA-specific checks

  R/lantern_load.R — Fixes package-name construction for ROCm cudatoolkit packages; adds tryCatch around lib_path() to prevent startup failures; adds Windows cuDNN PATH prepend.
